title: YoCierge vs ChartRequest vs Codes Health
summary: Compare YoCierge, ChartRequest, and Codes Health for medical record retrieval in 2026, covering AI analysis, integrations, completeness checks, and flat fee pricing for plaintiff firms.
body_markdown:
Personal injury law firms lose countless billable hours chasing medical records through phone calls, faxes, and provider portals. Traditional retrieval vendors deliver documents, but the real work begins when paralegals spend many hours per case manually reviewing thousands of pages for pre-existing conditions, treatment gaps, and damages documentation.[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) takes a fundamentally different approach by combining AI-powered retrieval with human-verified analysis, delivering litigation-ready case intelligence rather than raw documents. This comparison looks at how Codes Health stacks up against YoCierge and ChartRequest across features, workflow integration, and total cost of ownership for plaintiff law firms.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


Codes Health pairs AI-powered case chronologies with litigation-focused analysis, including potential breach-of-care indicators, missing record detection, and human-verified insights, all inside its flat fee


-


YoCierge offers a broad case management integration ecosystem spanning more than 12 platforms, while Codes Health focuses on a native embedded partnership with Filevine that keeps retrieval workflow inside the case file


-


ChartRequest maintains the largest documented provider network at 12,000+ healthcare organizations, though Codes Health provides nationwide coverage through multiple retrieval channels


-


Incomplete authorizations are a leading cause of denied record requests, and Codes Health's AI validation catches missing signatures, incorrect dates, and unchecked boxes before submission


-


Human verification of AI outputs distinguishes Codes Health from pure automation platforms, addressing accuracy concerns that matter for litigation-grade analysis


-


Codes Health works toward complete, organized records in a couple of weeks, rather than the months manual retrieval workflows often take


## **Understanding the Landscape of Medical Record Retrieval Software**


### **The Growing Demand for Specialized Retrieval Solutions**


Medical record retrieval has evolved from a purely administrative task into a strategic function for plaintiff law firms. The market is projected to grow from[$1.1 billion in 2024](https://www.insightaceanalytic.com/report/medical-records-retrieval-market/3042) to $2.8 billion by 2034, driven by increasing healthcare digitization and demand for faster turnaround times.


For personal injury attorneys, medical records directly influence:


-


Case qualification and intake decisions


-


Damages documentation and valuation


-


Demand letter preparation and negotiation leverage


-


Expert witness coordination


-


Trial strategy and courtroom presentation


Traditional retrieval workflows lean heavily on manual processes. Staff members call providers, send faxes, track responses in spreadsheets, and follow up repeatedly until records arrive. That approach creates bottlenecks that delay case progression and eats paralegal time better spent on higher-value work.


### **Why Retrieval Platform Selection Matters**


Not all retrieval platforms serve legal teams equally. Many solutions originated in healthcare settings, where the goal is patient intake rather than litigation support. These platforms deliver raw records but leave firms responsible for:


-


Building chronologies from thousands of unorganized pages


-


Identifying pre-existing conditions that defense counsel will raise


-


Documenting treatment gaps and missed appointments


-


Calculating future medical expenses for damages analysis


-


Flagging potential breaches in care for medical malpractice screening


The distinction between document delivery and case intelligence defines the competitive landscape. Some platforms focus on retrieval speed. Others prioritize provider network breadth. A newer generation combines retrieval operations with AI-powered analysis to reduce the manual review burden.


## **Codes Health: An AI-Powered Solution for Streamlined Medical Records**


### **The AI-Human Hybrid Approach**


[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) operates an AI-powered platform that handles both medical record retrieval and case analysis for plaintiff law firms. Founded in 2024 and backed by[Y Combinator](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/codes-health) , Amplify Partners, General Catalyst, Haystack, Night Capital, and Pathlight Ventures, the company positions itself as a "premier pre-litigation department without the overhead."


The platform's hybrid approach combines automated AI processing with human verification. AI-generated insights are reviewed by medical and legal experts before delivery. That addresses a real concern in legal technology: AI systems can produce compelling but inaccurate outputs. General AI platforms such as ChatGPT are not designed for litigation-grade medical record review, and using them on clinical documentation risks confident answers that fall apart under scrutiny. Codes Health's platform is purpose-built for this work and analyzes medical records with high precision, with expert verification layered on top before anything reaches the case file.


### **Tailored Analysis for Legal Practice Areas**


Unlike generic medical summary tools, Codes Health tailors its analysis to specific legal contexts. For personal injury cases, the platform identifies:


-


Pre-existing conditions that defense counsel will scrutinize


-


Treatment gaps and missed appointments


-


Documented future medical expenses


-


Care patterns relevant to damages calculation


-


Potential breaches in standard of care


This context-aware analysis cuts into the manual review time paralegals typically spend on each case. Rather than searching through every document for relevant facts, legal teams receive organized insights linked to source materials for verification.


Codes Health's MIT-educated engineering team keeps building out additional workflows and products, so the platform continues to evolve, improve, and grow more comprehensive as the demands of modern legal practices change.


## **YoCierge and ChartRequest: Alternative Solutions in Medical Document Retrieval**


### **YoCierge's Concierge Service Model**


YoCierge operates a high-touch concierge service model that emphasizes personal attention and relationship-based support. The company has been expanding its medical record locator service into additional states, including Nevada and Connecticut, as it works toward nationwide coverage.


Key YoCierge characteristics include:


-


Flat fee pricing without per-page charges


-


Same-day order processing for requests submitted before 4pm, which covers order handling rather than completed record delivery


-


Integration with more than 12 case management platforms including Clio, SmartAdvocate, MyCase, Smokeball, and Filevine


-


YoSign e-authorization tool for electronic signatures


-


Volume-based pricing structure


YoCierge primarily emphasizes retrieval, but it also offers AI-assisted record organization and summarization through features such as ReChron, ICD-10 extraction, and AI-generated medical record summaries. Codes Health differentiates its offering through broader litigation-focused analysis, including missing record detection, potential breach-of-care indicators, and human-verified case insights.


### **ChartRequest's Healthcare-Centric Platform**


ChartRequest, operating its legal division under the CaseBinder brand, brings a healthcare-centric approach to medical record retrieval. Originally designed to serve healthcare providers managing release of information requests, the platform has expanded to serve legal teams.


ChartRequest strengths include:


-


Network of 12,000+ healthcare organizations


-


Hybrid model combining technology with human support


-


Mobile app and dashboard for request tracking


-


System integrations drawn from healthcare market experience


-


Established track record since 2012


ChartRequest primarily emphasizes retrieval automation and human-supported fulfillment, and YoCierge also provides AI-assisted chronology and summarization features. ChartRequest's healthcare origins mean its workflows are optimized for provider-side operations rather than litigation-specific needs.


## **Achieving Speed and Efficiency: Codes Health's Retrieval Differentiators**


### **From Months to Weeks**


Traditional medical record retrieval can take 45 to 90 days through manual processes.[Codes Health works](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/best-chartrequest-alternatives) toward complete records in a couple of weeks through a combination of technology and persistent operational follow-up.


The platform reaches records through claims clearinghouses, patient portals, custodian integrations, and traditional retrieval channels. This multi-channel approach supports coverage regardless of how individual facilities handle record requests.


Speed claims deserve a closer look during vendor evaluation. According to Codes Health, services promising same-day retrieval typically return only the records sitting immediately available in electronic channels, which leaves the firm and the client chasing down everything else. That added client involvement, in the company's stated experience, is a common source of frustration and client churn. Codes Health does not market same-day retrieval. It works toward the complete record set, including the harder-to-reach providers, date ranges, and billing files, in a couple of weeks rather than months.


### **Proactive Error Prevention**


Incomplete authorizations are a leading cause of denied record requests. Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, and unchecked boxes for sensitive records can send a request back to the start and reset the response window that providers are working against.


Codes Health's AI review catches these errors before submission by automatically flagging:


-


Misspellings and missing or incomplete signatures


-


Missing or incorrect dates of service


-


Provider-specific requirement gaps


-


Authorization form errors that would otherwise cause provider rejections


This proactive approach prevents costly delays that compound across multi-provider cases. Rather than discovering authorization problems weeks later, firms catch issues immediately.


### **Persistent Provider Follow-Up**


Once requests are submitted, Codes Health manages ongoing provider outreach through calls, faxes, emails, and portal interactions. The platform tracks every communication attempt and provides visibility into completed outreach and next required actions.


That removes the burden of manually chasing providers. Staff do not need to check spreadsheets, make follow-up calls, or wonder about request status. The platform handles persistence while legal teams focus on case work.


## **HIPAA Compliance: A Cornerstone of Secure Medical Record Management**


### **Baseline Security Requirements**


Any platform handling protected health information must maintain HIPAA compliance. This is not a differentiator but a baseline requirement for legal technology in the medical records space.


It also helps to know the timeline the law actually sets. Under the federal HIPAA right of access, covered entities generally must respond to a records request within 30 calendar days, with one possible 30-day extension if the requester is notified. Some state laws set shorter deadlines, so firms working across jurisdictions should confirm the applicable standard rather than assuming the federal window.


Codes Health operates as a[HIPAA-compliant platform](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) with encryption in transit and at rest. The company provides secure document storage for retrieved materials and HIPAA-compliant e-signature workflows for authorization forms and releases of information.


### **Beyond Compliance Checkboxes**


Real security goes beyond compliance certifications. For law firms evaluating retrieval platforms, key considerations include:


-


Data residency and storage location controls


-


Audit logging and access tracking


-


Integration security with case management systems


-


Credential management for API connections


-


Incident response and breach notification procedures


Firms should request specific security documentation during vendor evaluation rather than taking compliance claims at face value.


## **Integration with Filevine: Codes Health's Strategic Partnership and Workflow**


### **Native Embedded Workflow**


On July 13, 2026, Filevine announced a strategic partnership with Codes Health.


The[partnership embeds](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/filevine) medical record retrieval directly into the Filevine case-management environment. This integration goes beyond typical third-party connections by positioning Codes Health as a premium service available where legal teams already manage their cases.


Filevine users can:


-


Submit record requests directly from case files


-


Track request status and provider outreach in real time


-


Communicate with the Codes Health team within the case workflow


-


Receive completed medical records, billing records, and imaging delivered into the Filevine project


-


Review retrieval history and completeness status without switching systems


### **Reducing Context Switching**


Traditional retrieval means moving between case management platforms, vendor portals, email, and downloaded file folders. Each transition creates friction and increases the risk of information falling through cracks.


With the Filevine integration, everything stays connected to the relevant case file. Requests, communications, documents, and billing remain in one place. That reduces context switching and helps maintain a single operational record for each matter.


For firms using other case management platforms, Codes Health can build custom integrations with CRM platforms and other medical software for high-volume customers, extending workflow benefits beyond the Filevine ecosystem.


## **Optimizing Legal Workflows with Codes Health's AI Capabilities**


### **Automated Case Chronologies**


Medical records arrive as hundreds or thousands of pages from multiple providers.[Codes Health automatically](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/tavrn-vs-chartrequest-vs-codes-health) organizes and compiles these records into case chronologies, grouping patient encounters and bills by visit.


This automation addresses a significant paralegal burden. Manual chronology creation means reading every document, identifying relevant events, and organizing it all into a usable format, and the time savings compound across case volumes.


Chronology automation also exposes documentation gaps. When records from certain date ranges or facilities are missing, the organized view makes those gaps visible right away. Firms can request specific missing records rather than repeating broad retrieval requests.


### **Extracting Actionable Insights**


Beyond organization, Codes Health's AI extracts structured information from unstructured medical records:


-


Diagnoses and treatment history


-


Provider names and dates of service


-


Medical expenses documented in records


-


Future medical needs mentioned by treating physicians


-


Care events relevant to case theory


For medical malpractice screening, the platform[flags potential breaches](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/tavrn-vs-yocierge-vs-codes-health) in standard of care. That capability speeds up case evaluation for attorneys who need to identify negligence indicators quickly.


The platform also includes a copilot-style interface that lets users ask questions about patient history rather than manually searching every document.


## **Comprehensive Record Retrieval: Medical, Billing, and Imaging Support**


### **Beyond Clinical Records**


Litigation requires more than clinical notes. Damages analysis depends on billing records that document treatment costs. Imaging studies provide visual evidence of injuries. Codes Health[supports medical, billing](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/software-solutions-law-firms) , and imaging requests through its platform.


This consolidates documentation needs. Firms do not need separate vendors or workflows for different record types, and everything flows through one platform with consistent tracking and delivery.


### **Ensuring Record Completeness**


Codes Health includes a[Missing Record Review](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/tavrn-vs-yocierge-vs-codes-health) feature that cross-references patient medical histories to identify documentation gaps. The AI flags when expected records are missing before the retrieval process closes.


This proactive completeness check heads off trial surprises. Discovering missing records during depositions or trial preparation creates significant problems. Catching gaps early leaves time for supplemental requests.


When records appear incomplete, the service works with facilities to resolve identified gaps before returning the completed set. That expands the value proposition from document acquisition to verified completeness.


## **Target Markets and Competitive Edge for Codes Health**


### **Legal Practice Area Focus**


Codes Health serves seven legal practice areas where medical records drive case outcomes:


-


Personal injury


-


Mass torts


-


Medical malpractice


-


Workers' compensation


-


Disability law


-


Insurance litigation


-


Wrongful death


Personal injury firms represent a core segment because medical documentation influences every phase from intake through trial. Mass tort practices benefit from scalable AI analysis across large plaintiff portfolios. Medical malpractice attorneys use chronologies and breach-of-care flagging to support expert review.


### **The Value Proposition Summarized**


The[total cost](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/blogs/best-chartrequest-alternatives) of ownership comparison favors platforms that eliminate separate chronology vendor fees. Traditional retrieval followed by outsourced chronology creation can add hundreds of dollars per case on top of retrieval costs.


Codes Health's flat fee includes:


-


Medical, billing, and imaging record retrieval


-


AI-powered case chronologies


-


Human-verified analysis and insights extraction


-


Missing record detection


-


Authorization validation


-


Persistent provider follow-up


For firms currently paying separate vendors for retrieval and chronology services, consolidating under one platform reduces both hard costs and coordination overhead.


## **Making an Informed Choice: Selecting the Right Partner for Your Needs**


The right choice depends less on feature lists than on which part of your workflow is costing you. If the bottleneck is getting documents in the door and your team already has a chronology process that works, a retrieval-focused vendor may cover it. If the bottleneck is what happens after the PDFs arrive, you need a platform that handles analysis too.


Questions worth asking before you commit:


-


Does the quoted turnaround describe completed record delivery, or just how fast the order gets processed?


-


Are chronologies, insights extraction, and missing record checks included, or billed separately?


-


Who verifies AI output before it reaches the case file?


-


What happens when a provider stops responding, and who does the chasing?


-


Does the platform work inside your case management system, or add another portal to log into?


### **Where Each Platform Fits**


YoCierge suits firms that value a concierge relationship, want broad case management integration options, and are comfortable pairing retrieval with AI-assisted organization and summaries.


ChartRequest suits firms that prioritize documented provider network breadth and a hybrid human-plus-technology fulfillment model.


Codes Health suits plaintiff firms that want retrieval, validation, completeness verification, and litigation-focused analysis handled together, under one flat fee, without standing up a separate chronology workflow.


## **The Bottom Line**


Most medical records problems that blow up a case were preventable months earlier. An authorization goes out with an unchecked box for sensitive records and comes back denied. A fast delivery looks complete until the billing file and the specialist records turn out to be missing, and now the client is making phone calls. A chronology gets built by hand, and the treatment gap defense counsel eventually raises was sitting on page 1,400 the whole time.


Codes Health is built for exactly those failure modes: validation that catches authorization errors before submission, persistent follow-up that pursues the complete record set in a couple of weeks rather than whatever arrives fastest, missing record detection that surfaces gaps before trial prep, and human-verified analysis that flags pre-existing conditions, treatment gaps, and potential breaches of care. All of it sits inside one flat fee.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **How does Codes Health handle records from facilities that do not participate in electronic record exchanges?**


Codes Health uses multiple retrieval channels including traditional fax, email, telephone follow-up, and direct provider portal access alongside claims clearinghouse and custodian integrations. When electronic channels are unavailable, the platform manages manual retrieval through persistent operational follow-up. This multi-channel approach supports nationwide coverage regardless of individual facility technology capabilities.


### **What happens if Codes Health's AI analysis identifies an error or discrepancy in the medical records?**


AI-generated outputs undergo human verification by medical and legal experts before delivery. When discrepancies show up between records from different providers, or potential documentation errors get flagged, the verification team reviews the source materials and notes the issues for the legal team's attention. The platform does not alter original records but provides organized insights that highlight areas requiring attorney review.


### **Can firms use Codes Health if they do not use Filevine for case management?**


Yes. While the Filevine integration provides the most seamless workflow experience, Codes Health serves firms using various case management platforms. For high-volume customers, the company can build custom integrations with CRM platforms and other medical software. Firms without integrated workflows can still access the platform's retrieval and analysis capabilities directly.


### **How does Codes Health's pricing compare for firms with varying case volumes?**


Codes Health uses flat fee pricing that includes retrieval and analysis in a single cost structure. The company does not publicly disclose specific rates, but the flat fee model eliminates per-page charges and surprise costs. Firms should contact Codes Health directly to discuss pricing based on their specific volume and practice area needs.


### **What training or onboarding does Codes Health provide for new customers?**


The platform is designed for intuitive use with minimal training requirements. For Filevine users, the embedded integration means staff members work within their familiar case management environment. Codes Health provides visibility into request status, completed outreach, and next actions without requiring separate vendor portal expertise. Firms can communicate with the Codes Health team directly through the platform for support during implementation and ongoing use.
